stem.text: Find the interval of convergence of the power series \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} \frac{3 x^{n}}{5^{n}} \). Use the ratio test for the interior and justify the behaviour at each endpoint.

answer_key.label: The interval of convergence is \( -5 < x < 5 \).

worked_solution.text: For the ratio test, form \( \left|\frac{\frac{3 x^{n+1}}{5^{n+1}}}{\frac{3 x^{n}}{5^{n}}}\right| \).
The series converges when \( \frac{\left|x\right|}{5} < 1 \), that is \( \left|x\right| < 5 \), so \( -5 < x < 5 \).

At \( x = 5 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} 3 \), which diverges by the nth term test, since every term equals 3. At \( x = -5 \) the series is \( \sum_{n=2}^{\infty} 3 (-1)^n \), which diverges by the nth term test, since its terms do not approach 0.
The interval of convergence is \( -5 < x < 5 \).

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( -5 \le x < 5 \).
options.derivation: the endpoint series with alternating signs tested with the alternating series test although its terms do not approach 0, and called convergent

options.label: The interval of convergence is \( x < 5 \).
options.derivation: the absolute value dropped when solving, so x < 5 was kept as the whole solution and only the endpoint 5 tested
